# with the versions of the geosense environment (Python 3.11.15). Edit the .in file, not this one.
# requirements-backend.in - Phase 5, Exercise 2 (Part C.3): what the backend container needs.
# Hand-trimmed from requirements.txt to the packages that mcp_server.py and the modules it
# imports (site_scorer, image_classifier, lidar_analyzer, streetview_semantic, tools/*)
# actually load. deploy/pin_requirements.py turns this list into requirements-backend.txt,
# pinning every package to the version installed in the geosense environment, so that the
# container runs exactly the versions the tools were tested with (the site-scorer pickle
# in particular must be opened by the scikit-learn and numpy that wrote it).
#
# Left out on purpose (never imported by the server): the training and download stacks of
# Phases I-III - xgboost, seaborn, pytest, torchgeo, albumentations, albucore, stringzilla,
# datasets, einops, geemap, scikit-image, opencv-python, tqdm (pulled in by shap anyway),
# tensorboard, open3d, segment-anything, pycocotools, accelerate, rasterio, GeoAlchemy2 -
# and the agent and Streamlit stack, which is the frontend image (requirements-frontend.in).
# PyTorch and torchvision are installed by the Dockerfile from the PyTorch CPU index
# (the cu128 build of the laptop would add about 3 GB of CUDA libraries a CPU container
# cannot use); the two lines below only record the versions.
